OPEN
This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $p_1<\cdots<p_u$ be primes and let $k\geq 1$. Let $F_k(p_1,\ldots,p_u)$ be such that every interval of $k$ positive integers contains at least $F_k(p_1,\ldots,p_u)$ multiples of at least one of the $p_i$.
Estimate $F_k(p_1,\ldots,p_u)$, particularly in the range $k=\alpha p_u$ for constant $\alpha>2$.
#1143: [Va99,1.8]
number theory | 
primes
In [Va99] it is reported that Erdős and Selfridge found 'the exact bound' when $2<\alpha<3$, and that 'if $\alpha>3$ then very little is known'. No reference is given, and I cannot find a relevant paper of Erdős and Selfridge.
See also [970].

 With GPT-5.5 Pro I've got a nice connection of this problem to the inverse arithmetic Kakeya problem and [1097].
This allows to establish a partial result with some lower bounds unconditionally like\[
 F_{\lfloor\alpha p_u\rfloor}(p_1,\ldots,p_u)\gg u^{6/11}\qquad(\alpha\geq3)
\]Here is the note.

 Thanks, yes; this is exactly (one of) the equivalences of the arithmetic Kakeya conjecture found by Green and Ruzsa. (I really should have noticed this, since I know that paper quite well, but clearly the notation in this case is different enough that this didn't jump out at me at the time.)
The Green-Ruzsa paper also cites earlier work of Erdős and Selfridge, which clarifies what [Va99] was referring to; I'll update the site accordingly.
